concepts.name: Set Theory & Cartesian Products
concepts.description: Fundamental set operations (Union, Intersection, Cartesian products) forming relational algebra.

questions.question: If Table A has 3 rows and Table B has 4 rows, how many rows will a Cartesian Product (CROSS JOIN) return?
questions.explanation: A Cartesian product pairs every row of Table A with every row of Table B: 3 * 4 = 12 rows.

questions.question: What is the difference between UNION and UNION ALL in SQL set operations?
options: UNION eliminates duplicate rows; UNION ALL keeps all rows including duplicates
UNION ALL eliminates duplicates; UNION keeps duplicates
UNION only works on tables with numeric columns
There is no difference in modern relational databases
questions.correct_answer: UNION eliminates duplicate rows; UNION ALL keeps all rows including duplicates
questions.explanation: UNION runs a deduplication step which incurs performance overhead, whereas UNION ALL directly concatenates sets.

concepts.name: Primary & Foreign Keys
concepts.description: Understanding unique identifiers, integrity constraints, and relational table references.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a Foreign Key constraint in a relational database?
options: To ensure the table has unique column names
To enforce referential integrity between two related tables
To make queries execute faster without indexes
questions.correct_answer: To enforce referential integrity between two related tables
questions.explanation: A Foreign Key enforces referential integrity by ensuring a value matches a Primary Key in another table.

questions.question: An attempt to delete a record in the 'departments' table fails with a Foreign Key violation error. Why does this happen?
options: Records in another table (e.g. 'employees') reference this department id
The department record has null values
The database server ran out of disk space
questions.correct_answer: Records in another table (e.g. 'employees') reference this department id
questions.explanation: Foreign Key constraints prevent orphaned records by blocking deletions of parent records that child tables still reference.

concepts.name: SQL Basic Queries (SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY)
concepts.description: Extracting and filtering data using SELECT, FROM, WHERE, and sorting with ORDER BY.

questions.question: Which clause filters rows BEFORE an aggregation operation in SQL?
questions.explanation: WHERE filters individual records before aggregation; HAVING filters aggregated groups.

questions.question: Which query correctly returns the top 5 highest-paid employees?
options: SELECT * FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 5;
SELECT * FROM employees WHERE salary = MAX(salary) LIMIT 5;
SELECT TOP 5 * FROM employees SORT salary;
SELECT * FROM employees ORDER BY salary ASC LIMIT 5;
questions.correct_answer: SELECT * FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 5;
questions.explanation: ORDER BY salary DESC sorts from highest to lowest, and LIMIT 5 extracts the top 5 rows.

concepts.name: SQL Joins (INNER, LEFT, RIGHT, FULL)
concepts.description: Combining records from two or more tables based on a related key column.

questions.question: You need a report listing ALL customers and their orders, including customers who have not placed any orders yet. Which join should you use?
options: SELECT * FROM Customers c INNER JOIN Orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
SELECT * FROM Customers c LEFT JOIN Orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
SELECT * FROM Customers c CROSS JOIN Orders o
SELECT * FROM Customers c RIGHT JOIN Orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
questions.correct_answer: SELECT * FROM Customers c LEFT JOIN Orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
questions.explanation: LEFT JOIN retains all records from the left table (Customers) even when no match exists in Orders.

questions.question: If Table A has IDs [1, 2, 3] and Table B has IDs [2, 3, 4], which IDs will be returned by an INNER JOIN on ID?
questions.explanation: INNER JOIN returns strictly matching records present in both tables: 2 and 3.

concepts.name: SQL Aggregation & GROUP BY
concepts.description: Summarizing data using COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX and grouping with GROUP BY / HAVING.

questions.question: To find departments having more than 5 employees with average salary > 60,000, which clause filters the average salary?
questions.explanation: HAVING is used to filter aggregate conditions like AVG(salary) > 60000 after grouping.

questions.question: What is the outcome of `COUNT(*)` vs `COUNT(column_name)` when a column contains NULL values?
options: COUNT(*) counts all rows; COUNT(column_name) ignores NULL values
Both return the exact same count always
COUNT(column_name) throws an error on NULLs
COUNT(*) ignores NULLs; COUNT(column_name) counts NULLs
questions.correct_answer: COUNT(*) counts all rows; COUNT(column_name) ignores NULL values
questions.explanation: COUNT(*) counts total rows in the group, whereas COUNT(col) counts only non-null instances.

concepts.name: SQL Window Functions (OVER, PARTITION BY, RANK)
concepts.description: Advanced analytical calculations across a set of table rows related to the current row without collapsing rows.

questions.question: What is the key difference between RANK() and DENSE_RANK() when two rows have equal values?
options: RANK() leaves gaps in rank numbers for ties; DENSE_RANK() does not leave gaps
DENSE_RANK() leaves gaps; RANK() does not leave gaps
RANK() only works with numeric columns; DENSE_RANK() works with text
There is no difference in PostgreSQL
questions.correct_answer: RANK() leaves gaps in rank numbers for ties; DENSE_RANK() does not leave gaps
questions.explanation: RANK() assigns 1, 2, 2, 4 (leaves gap); DENSE_RANK() assigns 1, 2, 2, 3 (no gap).

questions.question: Which window function clause computes a running cumulative total of revenue by date for each product category?
options: SUM(revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY date)
questions.correct_answer: SUM(revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY date)
questions.explanation: PARTITION BY resets the running calculation for each category, and ORDER BY date computes the cumulative sum chronologically.

concepts.name: Python Fundamentals (Variables, Control Flow)
concepts.description: Basic syntax, conditionals, loops, functions, and error handling in Python.

questions.question: What will be the output of `bool([])` in Python?
questions.explanation: Empty collections (lists, dicts, tuples, strings) evaluate to False in Python truth-value testing.

questions.question: What is the output of `[x ** 2 for x in range(4) if x % 2 == 0]`?
questions.explanation: range(4) is 0, 1, 2, 3. The even numbers are 0 and 2. 0^2 = 0, 2^2 = 4.

concepts.name: Python Data Structures (Lists, Dicts, Sets)
concepts.description: Manipulating lists, dictionaries, tuples, and sets with comprehensions.

questions.question: What is the average time complexity of looking up a key in a Python dictionary?
questions.explanation: Python dictionaries are implemented as hash tables, giving them average O(1) time complexity for lookups.

questions.question: Which data structure in Python is immutable and hashable, making it valid as a dictionary key?
questions.explanation: Tuples are immutable; if their elements are also hashable, they can serve as dictionary keys.

concepts.name: Pandas DataFrames & Series
concepts.description: Loading, inspecting, and selecting data using Pandas DataFrames and Series.

questions.question: In Pandas, what is the primary difference between `df.loc[]` and `df.iloc[]`?
options: loc is label-based; iloc is integer position-based
iloc is label-based; loc is integer position-based
loc works on columns only; iloc works on rows only
loc modifies the DataFrame in-place; iloc returns a copy
questions.correct_answer: loc is label-based; iloc is integer position-based
questions.explanation: `.loc[]` indexes by explicit index/column labels, while `.iloc[]` indexes by 0-based integer positions.

questions.question: Which command filters DataFrame `df` for rows where column 'age' is greater than 30 and 'city' is 'Mumbai'?
questions.explanation: Pandas requires bitwise operators (`&`, `|`) with explicit parenthetical conditions for element-wise boolean indexing.

concepts.name: Data Cleaning & Imputation (Pandas)
concepts.description: Handling missing values, deduplication, type casting, and string manipulation.

questions.question: When replacing missing values in a numeric column skewed by heavy outliers, which imputation statistic is most robust?
questions.explanation: Median is the 50th percentile and is resistant to extreme outliers, whereas the mean is heavily pulled by skew.

questions.question: Which method drops rows only if ALL columns in that row are NaN in Pandas?
questions.explanation: `how='all'` ensures a row is dropped only if every single value in that row is missing.

concepts.name: Descriptive Statistics (Mean, Median, Variance, IQR)
concepts.description: Measures of central tendency, dispersion, variance, standard deviation, and quartiles.

questions.question: In a right-skewed (positively skewed) distribution, which inequality typically holds true?
questions.explanation: Positive skew pulls the mean to the right (tail), so Mean > Median > Mode.

questions.question: What percentage of data lies between the First Quartile (Q1) and Third Quartile (Q3) in any distribution?
questions.explanation: The Interquartile Range (IQR = Q3 - Q1) covers the middle 50% of the observations.

concepts.name: Inferential Statistics & Hypothesis Testing
concepts.description: Null hypothesis, p-values, t-tests, ANOVA, and confidence intervals.

questions.question: A p-value of 0.02 is obtained with a significance threshold (alpha) of 0.05. What is the appropriate statistical decision?
options: Fail to reject the Null Hypothesis (H0)
Accept the Null Hypothesis as 100% proven
Increase the sample size and repeat
questions.explanation: Since p-value (0.02) < alpha (0.05), we reject the null hypothesis in favor of the alternative.

questions.question: What is a Type I error in hypothesis testing?
options: Rejecting the null hypothesis when it is actually true (False Positive)
Failing to reject the null hypothesis when it is false (False Negative)
Using a t-test instead of an ANOVA
questions.correct_answer: Rejecting the null hypothesis when it is actually true (False Positive)
questions.explanation: Type I error (alpha) occurs when we falsely reject a true null hypothesis.

concepts.name: Data Visualization & Chart Selection
concepts.description: Choosing the right chart type (Bar, Line, Scatter, Heatmap) for categorical vs continuous distributions.

questions.question: Which visualization type is best suited to display the correlation between two continuous numeric variables?
questions.explanation: A scatter plot maps two continuous variables on Cartesian coordinates (X and Y), revealing correlation patterns.

questions.question: You need to show monthly revenue trends over the past 3 years. Which chart type is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Line charts excel at showing continuous trends, changes, and seasonality over time.

concepts.name: BI Dashboards & Metric Hierarchy
concepts.description: Designing clear KPI executive summaries, drill-down interactivity, and cognitive load reduction.

questions.question: Which principle best reduces cognitive overload on an executive analytics dashboard?
options: Display 20+ charts simultaneously on the primary screen
Show top-level North Star KPIs first, followed by drill-down filters for detail
Use 10 distinct bright colors across charts
Replace all numbers with 3D pie charts
questions.correct_answer: Show top-level North Star KPIs first, followed by drill-down filters for detail
questions.explanation: Executive dashboards adhere to progressive disclosure: high-level summary KPIs at a glance, with on-demand drill-down.

questions.question: In visual perception theory (Edward Tufte), what does the 'Data-Ink Ratio' represent?
options: Proportion of ink used to display actual data vs total ink in the graphic
The resolution of print ink used for charts
The number of colors used in a dashboard
The font size of axis labels
questions.correct_answer: Proportion of ink used to display actual data vs total ink in the graphic
questions.explanation: Tufte defines Data-Ink Ratio as data-ink divided by total ink used; higher is better because it minimizes chart clutter.
